stem: A 6-year-old girl is being reviewed for possible unhealthy excess weight. Her father asks why the clinician is plotting BMI on an age-based chart rather than using the number alone. What is the best explanation?

options.text: BMI is mainly used in children under 2 years of age
BMI is the standard tool for unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years because it depends on age and stage of growth
BMI can be interpreted in children the same way as in adults, without reference to age
BMI is only useful when weight is below the 3rd percentile
BMI is not used in paediatrics because length and height are more important

explanation: BMI is the standard tool for assessing unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years. This is because BMI must be interpreted on an age-based chart, since it varies with age and stage of growth rather than being a stand-alone number.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because BMI is used in children older than 2 years, not mainly in those under 2 years.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because BMI is the standard tool for unhealthy weight in children older than 2 years and must be interpreted in the context of age and stage of growth.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because BMI in children cannot be interpreted the same way as in adults without reference to age.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because BMI is used for assessing unhealthy weight generally, not only when weight is below the 3rd percentile.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because BMI is used in paediatrics for children older than 2 years and is interpreted alongside growth information.
